message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and the fundamentals supported a purchase within your mandate. Total net sales rose 2% to $391.0B, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2B, which lifted total gross margin to 46.2% (from 44.1%) and operating income to $123.2B; net income was $93.7B ($6.08 diluted EPS), depressed by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), and the company still generated $118.3B of operating cash flow and held $140.8B in cash and marketable securities. The soft spots — Greater China net sales down 8%, iPad down 6%, Wearables down 7%, and flat iPhone revenue — are offset by the high-margin Services mix shift, a $110B buyback authorization, and a rising dividend. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.90 — a limit just above the ask to ensure a fill while staying close to market — which executed at $222.90 for a total of $9,807.60. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap and brings today's total purchases to $9,807.60, well under the $20,000 daily limit; it is a buy of a permitted ticker, and no funds were moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares held).

Order filled at 222.90, 44 shares = $9,807.60. Total today $9,807.60 < $20,000. Good.
